data.title: These Are the Stocks Reporting Earnings Today – November 19, 2026
data.description:
Here's a look at today's key earnings reports from major publicly traded companies. Stock market investors will undoubtedly be watching closely for financial updates and surprises that could move the market. To dive deeper into any of the companies listed below, click on their ticker symbols, as TipRanks' unique datasets will help you research the stocks and decide whether they are a Buy, Sell, or Hold.

A.M. Earnings

(BABA), (WMT), (PDD), (NTES), (FUTU), (BBWI)

Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba is expected to report adjusted earnings of $1.63 per share on revenue of approximately $40.5 billion. The results come as the company invests heavily in artificial intelligence to expand its cloud business. Last quarter, revenue from its AI Cloud and Compute Services division grew by 45% to $7.14 billion.

However, Alibaba's capital expenditures also increased by 75% to nearly $10 billion. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings per share declined by 42% as the company continued to invest in its businesses. Therefore, today's report will show whether stronger AI demand is helping Alibaba offset the costs of its expansion.

Separately, retail giant Walmart is expected to report adjusted earnings of $0.64 per share on revenue of $187.38 billion. Last quarter, U.S. comparable sales increased by 2.6%, compared to 4.6% a year earlier. Interestingly, though, global e-commerce sales grew by 23%, while advertising revenue increased by 38%.

Walmart's growing advertising business is particularly important because it allows the retailer to earn revenue from brands that pay to promote their products. For today's report, Walmart previously forecast adjusted earnings between $0.62 and $0.64 per share. Its updated outlook for the holiday shopping season will also be important as the company prepares for its busiest sales period.

P.M. Earnings

(INTU), (ESTC), (KEYS), (GAP), (BULL), (ROST), (HP)

Financial software company Intuit is expected to report adjusted earnings of $2.46 per share on revenue of approximately $4.30 billion. The company, which owns QuickBooks and TurboTax, enters today's report after recording 14% revenue growth in Fiscal 2026. Within that period, QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue increased by 23%, while TurboTax Live revenue grew by 37%.

Nevertheless, Intuit expects total revenue growth to slow down to between 9% and 10% in Fiscal 2027, with sales reaching $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion. The company has also changed how it calculates adjusted earnings by including stock-based compensation expenses, which makes direct comparisons with last year's adjusted earnings less straightforward.

data.title: Nvidia Courts Arm CEO Rene Haas to Replace Jensen Huang
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) has approached Arm (ARM) CEO Rene Haas as a possible replacement for Jensen Huang, according to Bloomberg. The chipmaker has yet to make a formal offer, and Haas has not accepted the role. Nvidia continues its search for a permanent candidate, with Colette Kress currently serving as interim CEO.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Nvidia hired Heidrick & Struggles to find its next CEO. The firm has reportedly spoken with potential candidates, including Haas.

Haas Background at Nvidia

Haas spent seven years at Nvidia, from 2006 to 2013, rising to vice president and general manager of computing products. He joined Arm in 2013 and became its CEO in February 2022. Nvidia also tried to acquire Arm in 2020, but the deal fell through amid regulatory opposition.

Speaking at a tech conference in Austin on Wednesday, Haas described his former boss as "a legend." "What he built at Nvidia is historic; you don't have many champions like that," Haas said.

Other potential candidates include Nvidia Vice President Ian Buck, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) CEO Lisa Su, and Apple (AAPL) Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji. President Donald Trump has also floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking the job.

Nvidia Without Huang

Nvidia cut ties with Huang on November 12 after revelations about his extramarital affairs triggered a widening scandal. Huang has admitted to a relationship with a woman who has been investigated by the U.S. government over alleged spying for China.

Huang led Nvidia for more than 30 years. The company wants to show investors it can keep growing without Huang. Nvidia also held a meeting with employees on Wednesday. Interim CEO Colette Kress sought to reassure staff with a simple message: "We've got this."

Nvidia is also pointing to its strong financial performance. In Q3 FY27, EPS came in at $2.68, beating estimates of $2.48. Revenue surged 103% year-over-year to $115.8 billion, topping expectations of $108.97 billion. Data Center revenue jumped 110% to $107.6 billion, accounting for about 93% of total sales.

Is NVDA Stock a Buy?

Nvidia's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell issued in the past three months. The average NVDA price target of $232.59 implies 54% upside from current levels.

data.title: Markets Gear Up for Anthropic's $1.5 Trillion IPO
data.description:
U.S. stock futures traded higher ahead of Thursday's market open as investors focused on Anthropic's (ANT) highly anticipated Nasdaq debut. The Claude maker is targeting a potential $1.5 trillion valuation, which would make it one of the largest IPOs in history.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 1.33%, 0.82%, and 0.51%, respectively, as of 1:40 a.m. EST on November 19.

Anthropic has priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initial target range of $70 to $78, following strong investor demand. The company also increased the offering size from 825 million to 980 million shares. The IPO is expected to raise approximately $81.34 billion, surpassing SpaceX's (SPCX) $75 billion June offering to become the largest IPO on record.

Meanwhile, oil prices were mixed in Asian trading on Thursday after falling in the previous session. Concerns about rising oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates weighed on prices, offsetting concerns about supply disruptions amid continued attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Higher interest rates could slow the economy and cut oil demand. Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting added to bets that it could raise rates in December to curb inflation.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.29% to $92.21 per barrel, while WTI crude futures fell 0.11% to $83.17 per barrel.

During Wednesday's regular trading session, the three major U.S. indexes closed mixed. The DJIA fell 1.11%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.23%, marking its fifth straight day of losses. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.

Looking ahead, investors will also watch data on weekly jobless claims for further clues about the strength of the U.S. labor market. On the earnings front, results from Walmart (WMT), Alibaba (BABA), and Gap (GAP) are scheduled for release today.

data.title: Palo Alto Stock (PANW) Soars on $4.5B Applied Compute Deal and Solid Q1 Beat
data.description:
Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock soared more than 9% in Wednesday's after-hours trading after the cybersecurity company announced a $4.5 billion deal to acquire AI startup Applied Compute and strong fiscal-first quarter results. The company's solid outlook and the news of the strategic deal come as cyberattacks rise amid the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI).

Palo Alto's Q1 FY27 revenue grew 39% year-over-year to $3.44 billion. The company now expects full-year FY27 revenue ⁠in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, compared with its previous forecast of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion.

More on Palo Alto's Acquisition of Applied Compute

Palo Alto is acquiring Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion. Applied Compute specializes in post-training and inference of open-weight AI models. Yash Patil, Applied Compute's co-founder and CEO, will become Palo Alto's co-chief AI officer after the completion of the acquisition. Palo Alto expects the deal to be completed in Q3 FY27. The company expects Applied Compute to add over $1 billion to its next-gen security annual recurring revenue (NGS ARR) by FY29. 

Open-weight models enable the user to customize the model's behavior, while closed models offered by Anthropic (ANT) and OpenAI retain greater control over how the model responds. On the earnings call, Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted that open-weight models have grown from under 5% of token traffic to more than 60% over the past year. The company expects the Applied Compute deal to help customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their AI use.

"We expect a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars of enterprise applications driven by open-weight and open-source adoption," said Arora.

Palo Alto has been making strategic deals to capitalize on growth opportunities in cybersecurity. The company's recent deals include the $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm ​Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi.

Baird Reacts to Palo Alto's Q1 Print

Following the Q1 FY27 print and news of the deal, Baird analyst Shrenik Kothari reiterated a Buy rating on Palo Alto stock with a price target of $420. The 5-star analyst said that the company reported "stellar" results, with better-than-expected guidance across NGS ARR, RPO (remaining performance obligation), and revenue.

Regarding the Applied Compute acquisition, Kothari believes that the deal deepens Palo Alto's presence in the AI development and inference stack, potentially enhancing its role beyond securing AI workloads to supporting the infrastructure used to build and operate them, "although monetization, integration remain open."

Is PANW a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Given robust AI-led demand tailwinds, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Palo Alto Networks stock based on 32 Buys and eight Holds. The average PANW stock price target of $411.76 indicates 21% upside potential.

These ratings and price targets could change as more analysts react to the results and the Applied Compute deal.

data.title: Amazon's Anthropic Stake Is Worth $159 Billion – What It Means for AMZN Stock
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) has a stake in Anthropic  (ANT) worth about $159 billion after the AI company priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share. Amazon invested $18 billion in Anthropic over three years. Its holding is now worth nearly nine times that amount on paper.

Anthropic priced its IPO above the earlier range of $70 to $78 per share. The offering covered 980 million shares and raised about $81.3 billion, making it the largest IPO on record. Anthropic has also arranged a separate $26 billion private placement with major tech companies. Its shares are set to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, November 19, under the ticker ANT.

Amazon's Anthropic Stake Adds About $15 per Share

Amazon's stake is equivalent to about $15 for each Amazon share. The company holds 1.92 billion non-voting Anthropic shares, equal to a 14.7% stake. At the IPO price of $83 per share, the holding is worth about $159 billion.

The $15 estimate uses Amazon's 10.81 billion shares outstanding. It equals about 5.5% of Amazon's market value at Wednesday's close of $267.74. This figure may change once Anthropic shares begin trading.

For now, the gain exists only on paper unless Amazon sells its shares. Amazon has said it plans to hold the stake for the long term. CEO Andy Jassy also said the company did not invest in Anthropic to make a quick profit.

Anthropic's $110 Billion AWS Deal Adds to Amazon's AI Opportunity

The AWS deal gives Amazon a long-term tie-up with Anthropic. Anthropic has agreed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon Web Services (AWS) from May 2026 to April 2036. Under the deal, Anthropic must spend this amount regardless of its actual usage, subject to the agreement's terms.

That comes to about $11 billion a year. The deal gives AWS a steady source of income as demand for AI computing grows. Anthropic needs cloud services to train and run its Claude models. So, Amazon is both a major investor and a key cloud supplier to the AI company.

Anthropic's growth shows why it needs so much computing power. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion by October. Demand for Claude and its coding tool, Claude Code, helped drive this growth. But running these AI tools also costs a lot. Reuters reported that Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing in the first half of 2026.

For Amazon, the deal adds a long-term source of business with Anthropic. The value of its stake will also depend on how ANT trades once public trading begins.

Is Amazon Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Amazon is Strong Buy, based on 42 Buy ratings and one Hold rating over the past three months. The average AMZN price target of $324.41 implies about 21% upside from current levels.
data.author: Shalu Saraf

data.title: Moody's Cuts Nvidia's Credit Outlook After Jensen Huang's Exit
data.description:
Moody's Ratings has lowered its credit outlook for Nvidia (NVDA) to Stable from Positive, citing concerns about the leadership change and the lack of a formal succession plan following the exit of longtime CEO Jensen Huang. The Stable outlook also means an upgrade is less likely over the next 12 to 18 months.

The move adds to the challenges facing the AI chip giant as it looks for a new leader. However, Moody's has kept its credit rating unchanged, reflecting the company's strong market position and financial health. A credit rating measures a company's ability to repay debt, while credit outlook indicates the likely direction of that rating in the future.

Leadership Change Raises Concerns

According to Moody's, Huang's exit has created uncertainty around Nvidia's business plans and financial policies. The agency also noted that the leadership change could affect the company's growth plans and its ties across the AI sector.

Huang left Nvidia on November 12 following reports about his personal ties to a woman who has been probed by U.S. authorities over alleged links to Chinese spying. The case has also brought greater scrutiny to the chipmaker.

Moody's Senior Vice President Raj Joshi said the leadership change could distract Nvidia's top team as it deals with the probes linked to the case.

Nvidia is now seeking a new CEO, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim head.

Credit Rating Remains Strong

Despite these concerns, Moody's kept Nvidia's Aa1 senior debt rating and Prime-1 short-term debt rating unchanged. Aa1 is the second-highest rating on Moody's scale and reflects the company's strong ability to meet its debt payments.

Moody's move does not point to a decline in Nvidia's business strength. The company remains a key player in AI chips and data center systems, backed by strong demand reflected in its September-quarter results.

NVDA Stock Movement

Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on November 12 following Huang's exit and lost another 4% on November 16 ahead of earnings. However, the stock rose nearly 5% in after-hours trading on November 17 after the company reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion and gave a strong sales forecast. The gains did not last, as shares fell 2.9% on November 18 amid several price target cuts from Wall Street. Investors remain concerned about whether Nvidia can keep growing at the same pace without Huang at the helm.

Will Nvidia Bounce Back?

On TipRanks, NVDA has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell rating. The average Nvidia price target of $232.59 implies 54.1% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: Nvidia vs. Alphabet: Wall Street Calls Only One AI Stock a 'Strong Buy' Ahead of Anthropic's IPO
data.description:
The approaching Nasdaq debut of Anthropic could offer an important test of investor appetite for AI, following weeks of turbulence among leading tech stocks. The ChatGPT rival priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, valuing the developer at $1.5 trillion ahead of Thursday's first session under ticker ANT. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) have each committed $10 billion to the company, giving both investors another reason to watch its reception closely.

Yet, the excitement surrounding Anthropic's IPO comes at a challenging time for its two biggest backers. Nvidia has plunged about 37% from its early October peak following Jensen Huang's departure, while Alphabet has shed 13% since its late-October earnings amid concerns over soaring AI spending. With both stocks struggling, investors may wonder whether Thursday's debut could finally give them a reason to turn bullish again.

Why Anthropic's IPO Could Be a Win for Nvidia and Alphabet Stocks

Anthropic's historic market debut could have implications far beyond its own valuation, especially for tech companies supplying the computing capacity behind its rapid expansion. As the first major U.S. frontier AI developer to enter public markets, Anthropic will give investors a clearer view of the industry's revenue potential, operating costs, and long-term profitability. Its performance could also influence how Wall Street values other companies benefiting from the AI boom.

For Nvidia and Alphabet, the opportunity extends beyond their respective $10 billion investments in Anthropic, with both companies positioned to benefit from its future spending. Google's parent could generate additional revenue through its cloud infrastructure partnership, while Nvidia stands to benefit from demand for advanced processors supporting the developer's computing requirements. These relationships could create opportunities over the coming years, although Anthropic's financial obligations and uncertain profitability remain important risks for investors.

Top analyst Daniel Ives, who ranks among the top 4% of Wall Street analysts, sees broader implications in this week's offering. His bullish outlook comes as institutional orders were estimated at $400 billion, alongside nearly $100 billion in retail interest, suggesting that buyers remain eager for direct exposure to frontier-model developers.

Ives described the potential impact in a recent note to clients, writing: "At a time in which investors are very nervous on the overall tech trade and the Nvidia black cloud moment casts a shadow over the tech sector, Anthropic's IPO is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI Revolution growth thesis is not waning."

Beyond that immediate boost, Ives anticipates $3 trillion to $4 trillion in industry spending over the next several years, supporting demand for chips, data facilities, and cloud capacity.

Nvidia vs. Alphabet: Which AI Giant Gets Wall Street's 'Strong Buy' Rating?

Wall Street's outlook for Nvidia remains positive, although recent downgrades have left the stock with a less enthusiastic consensus than Alphabet. With 30 Buy ratings, 13 Holds, and one Sell, the semiconductor leader currently earns an overall Moderate Buy recommendation. Meanwhile, the average 12-month price target of $232.59 implies shares could appreciate about 54% from their current levels.

Alphabet, meanwhile, enjoys stronger support from Wall Street, earning a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys and just 4 Holds. However, its average 12-month price target of $398.88 suggests a potential gain of 41% over the next 12 months, falling short of Nvidia's projected upside. data.title: 'The Peak May Be Here,' Says Top Investor About Nvidia Stock
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock briefly looked ready for a comeback after delivering another strong earnings report, but concerns surrounding Jensen Huang's absence ultimately overshadowed the chip giant's financial performance. Its encouraging results and outlook initially sent shares soaring nearly 5.5%, suggesting investors were prepared to look beyond the former CEO's departure. However, that enthusiasm proved short-lived, with the stock reversing course to close Wednesday down 2.9%, extending its losses to about 37% from its early October peak.

At such a steep discount, some investors might be wondering whether Nvidia has finally become too tempting to ignore. However, before pulling the trigger, they may want to hear from investor Victor Dergunov, who ranks among the top 3% of stock experts on TipRanks.

Despite acknowledging the company's outstanding financial performance, Dergunov believes staying on the sidelines remains the safer choice, warning that its strongest growth years may already be behind it.

The investor focuses on three areas that could determine where NVDA shares go next: revenue growth, profitability, and spending by its largest customers. His conclusion offers little encouragement to those expecting a rebound anytime soon.

"The base case scenario is that 2026 will mark the peak in all three," Dergunov opined.

That outlook suggests Nvidia could face a prolonged cooling period, potentially limiting future investment returns despite continued operational success.

For now, however, Nvidia's financial performance remains outstanding. Its latest quarterly results included revenue growth exceeding 100% year-over-year for the second consecutive period. Meanwhile, Nvidia has raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%, up from its previous projection of 70%.

Yet, Dergunov sees reasons for caution, pointing toward the company's shrinking price-to-sales multiple despite repeated earnings beats. This trend suggests the market has become less willing to reward Nvidia's achievements with generous valuations.

Profitability presents another concern as the company prepares for higher expenses alongside weaker margins. The company expects GAAP gross margin to range between 71% and 72% next quarter, while operating costs are projected to climb toward $11 billion.

Looking further ahead, Nvidia expects gross margins to recover to between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028, although that would remain below the 74.8% reported in its latest quarter. Such developments, according to Dergunov, could weigh on earnings potential, regardless of continued strength in customer orders.

Perhaps the biggest concern, however, involves Nvidia's largest clients and their appetite for expensive computing infrastructure. Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Oracle have poured billions into expanding data centers, helping drive the semiconductor manufacturer's extraordinary sales figures. Dergunov calculates that their combined capital expenditures have now exceeded operating cash flow, raising doubts about how long this pace can continue. Should these tech companies begin moderating investments, Nvidia could face a tougher environment than its latest quarterly figures suggest.

Ultimately, Dergunov believes investors should distinguish between owning a successful enterprise and purchasing an attractive investment at current prices.

"Strong quarterly results do not mean above-market shareholder returns," the investor wrote.

For now, Dergunov assigns NVDA shares a Hold (i.e., Neutral) rating, suggesting investors may be better served waiting for greater clarity before committing additional capital. (To watch Dergunov's track record, click here)

Wall Street, however, remains more bullish on Nvidia's prospects, with the stock earning a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and just one Sell. Still, analysts were far more enthusiastic just two weeks ago, before a wave of downgrades brought the number of Hold recommendations to 13. Nonetheless, the average 12-month price target of $232.59 suggests an upside potential of 54% from current levels. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: Market Turns to Anthropic's IPO
data.description:
Stock futures are little changed as the market awaits the highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO) of artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic (ANT) on Nov. 19. Shares of the company behind the Claude chatbot are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Composite exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT."

Anthropic upsized its offering late on Nov. 18, saying in a statement that it is responding to strong demand for its stock among investors. In a press release, Anthropic said that it plans to sell 980 million shares at $83 each. The company had initially planned to sell 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78. But strong demand led Anthropic to increase its shares on offer and their price.

In the futures market, the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average was rising 0.12%, the benchmark S&P 500 index was up 0.35%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq was gaining 0.80%.

Anthropic's Big Day

With its upwardly revised offering, Anthropic is on track to raise $81.3 billion from its IPO, surpassing SpaceX (SPCX), which held a record IPO in June that raised $75 billion. The final valuation of Anthropic is expected to be slightly above the $1.4 trillion that it was targeting in the share sale.

Investors and analysts now wait to see how ANT stock performs in its market debut. Market commentators quoted in The Wall Street Journal and Barron's say the IPO is a test for the AI industry, which has experienced volatility in recent weeks as concerns grow about the sustainability of the money being spent on data centers and other infrastructure.

Big Losses at Anthropic

In particular, there are concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and AI companies. Stocks of AI companies have also been volatile since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia (NVDA). Huang was seen as a champion and leader for the entire AI ecosystem.

While Anthropic is growing at a rapid rate, the company remains unprofitable. In its IPO prospectus, Anthropic said that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up 1,200% from the same period in 2025. But the company reported a $104 billion net loss during the first nine months of this year. That's up more than fourfold from the same stretch in 2025 when Anthropic reported a loss of $25 billion.

data.title: 3 'Strong Buy' High-Risk Stocks That Could Deliver 100% or More Gains
data.description:
Aurora Innovation (AUR), SanDisk Corp. (SNDK), and Praxis Precision Medicines (PRAX) are three high-risk, high-reward stocks analysts see as having massive upside potential. Wall Street rates each a Strong Buy and projects at least 100% upside. AUR leads the pack with about 193% upside potential.

These companies operate in fast-changing markets. In such markets, investor sentiment can shift quickly as conditions change. That volatility creates significant risk, but also the potential for huge gains. This is especially true if the companies deliver on their growth strategies.

These stocks have a beta greater than two. In other words, their shares are more than twice as volatile as the broader market.

Aurora Innovation (AUR)

Aurora is a U.S. self-driving tech startup known for the Aurora Driver. This advanced platform combines hardware, software, and data services to enable self-driving. Aurora was founded in 2017 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is now racing toward the commercial rollout of its technology.

On Wall Street, AUR has a Strong Buy consensus, with six Buys and two Holds issued over the past three months. The average AUR price target of $11.43 suggests about 193% upside ahead.

SanDisk Corp. (SNDK)

This is an American storage company. It develops and makes storage products based on NAND flash memory. This refers to non-volatile memory, meaning it stores data even when power is off. This technology is used in products such as solid-state drives, memory cards, and USB drives.

On Wall Street, SNDK carries a Strong Buy consensus, with 11 Buys and three Holds assigned over the past three months. This comes with an average price target of $2,131, suggesting about 175% upside.

Praxis Precision Medicines (PRAX)

Praxis is an American biopharma company. It makes drugs to treat brain and nerve conditions.

The company is currently seeking regulatory approval for its lead drug candidates. Relutrigine is designed to treat rare, severe seizure disorders. Similarly, ulixacaltamide is designed to treat uncontrollable shaking, especially in the hands.

On Wall Street, PRAX has a Strong Buy consensus rating. This reflects 13 Buys issued by analysts over the past three months. This comes with an average price target of $738.15, implying about 142% upside.
